text: Pathlib is the modern, object-oriented way to work with file paths, replacing clumsy string juggling.
You build a path by joining pieces with a slash — and pathlib overloads the division operator for exactly this.
It automatically uses the right separator for your operating system, so your code works everywhere.
[chuckle] A path object knows its own parts — the name, the file extension, the stem, and its parent folder.
No more fragile string splitting to pull apart a file path by hand.
[sniff] Path objects can check reality too — whether they exist, and whether they're a file or a directory.
[sigh] And glob finds every file matching a pattern, like all the Python files in a folder.
That turns directory searching into a single, readable loop.
[groan] Once you switch to pathlib, you'll never go back to gluing path strings together by hand.
